## Problem Statement

New users face a blank platform: the first workbench, first pipeline, and first
model deployment all start from empty forms, and time-to-first-success is
measured in days. We want a curated tutorial gallery in the Dashboard — a set
of maintained, tested tutorials (notebooks and pipelines) that users can launch
into their own project with one click. This requires product code (the gallery
and launch mechanics), authored content (the tutorials themselves), and
documentation — three different kinds of work with different owners and review
processes.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or importing the pipeline). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, first RAG app. Each is tested against the current release. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution process for new tutorials. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Notebooks
- Data Science Pipelines
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Partner- or community-contributed tutorial intake (contribution process is
  documented, but no submission tooling this release)
- Localization of tutorial content

## Open Questions

None.

# Define tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest)

## Description

This epic defines the tutorial packaging format that makes tutorials versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases. It produces the format specification — metadata describing each tutorial, pinned images, and a validation manifest — together with a reference package that demonstrates it. The format is the contract between the tutorial gallery (which renders and launches tutorials) and the tutorial content (which is authored and maintained separately), so both the gallery implementation and all tutorial authoring build on it.

## Scope

- Define the tutorial metadata model: the fields the gallery reads to present a tutorial (title, description, journey/category, kind — notebook or pipeline) and the fields needed for versioning.
- Define how tutorial images are pinned so a tutorial runs against known, tested image versions rather than floating tags.
- Define the validation manifest: the machine-readable description of how a tutorial is tested, so tutorial validation can run independently of Dashboard release cycles.
- Define the versioning scheme for tutorial packages, so a tutorial can be updated and re-tested without a Dashboard release.
- Produce a reference tutorial package that conforms to the format and passes the validation the manifest prescribes, as the worked example for content authors.
- Document the format for content authors (the authoring-facing spec; user-facing documentation is handled separately).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The packaging format specification is written and published where content authors and Dashboard developers can use it, covering metadata, pinned images, and the validation manifest.
- A reference tutorial package exists that conforms to the format and passes the validation defined by its own manifest.
- Versioning is demonstrated: a version bump of the reference package is expressed purely in package metadata, with no Dashboard change required.
- The gallery-facing consumption surface of the format (the metadata the gallery must read to list and launch a tutorial) is stable enough for the gallery implementation and tutorial authoring to proceed against it.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)**: A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases. This epic delivers HLR-3 in full.

# Dashboard tutorial gallery with one-click launch into user projects

## Description

This epic delivers the tutorial gallery in the Dashboard: a curated, browsable gallery of tutorials and the one-click launch mechanics that start a tutorial in the user's own project — opening a workbench pre-loaded with the tutorial notebook, or importing the tutorial pipeline into the project. It is the product-code work stream of the tutorial gallery strategy.

## Scope

- Add a tutorial gallery section to the Dashboard: listing curated tutorials with their metadata (title, description, journey) as defined by the tutorial packaging format.
- Implement one-click launch for notebook tutorials: from the gallery, start a workbench in the user's project with the tutorial notebook opened, using the existing workbench spawn flow and Notebook CR surface.
- Implement one-click launch for pipeline tutorials: from the gallery, import the tutorial pipeline into the user's project via the existing Data Science Pipelines import path (KFP v2 API).
- Read pinned image references from tutorial package metadata so launched tutorials use the tested image versions.
- Respect project context: tutorials launch into the project the user is working in, with no manual form filling beyond the single launch action.
- Gallery presentation details (navigation placement, empty states, progress feedback during launch) per Dashboard conventions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can open the tutorial gallery from the Dashboard and see the curated tutorials with their metadata.
- One click on a notebook tutorial opens a workbench in the user's project with the tutorial notebook available in it (validates the Notebooks component's existing workbench behavior end to end).
- One click on a pipeline tutorial imports that pipeline into the user's project (validates the Data Science Pipelines component's existing import path end to end).
- Launch uses the pinned images recorded in the tutorial package, not floating tags.
- End-to-end launch is verified against at least one packaged tutorial conforming to the tutorial packaging format, for each launch kind (workbench and pipeline import).
- No tutorial content is authored in this epic — the gallery renders and launches whatever conforms to the packaging format.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or importing the pipeline). This epic delivers HLR-1 in full.

# Author and test five notebook-based curated tutorials

## Description

This epic authors the notebook-based half of the curated tutorial suite — the content work stream of the tutorial gallery strategy. It produces five maintained, tested tutorials covering the core notebook journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first deployment, and first RAG app. Each tutorial is packaged and versioned per the tutorial packaging format and tested against the current release.

## Scope

- Author five notebook tutorials, each guiding a new user through one core journey:
  - First workbench — creating and using a first workbench.
  - Data prep — loading and preparing data in a workbench.
  - First training run — training a first model.
  - First deployment — deploying a first model for serving.
  - First RAG app — building a first retrieval-augmented generation application.
- Package each tutorial per the tutorial packaging format: metadata, pinned images, and a validation manifest.
- Write the validation defined by each tutorial's manifest and run it against the current release so each tutorial is verified to complete from a clean project.
- Keep tutorial content maintained: clear narrative steps, expected outcomes at each stage, and troubleshooting notes where new users commonly stall.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Five notebook tutorials exist, one per journey listed in Scope, each packaged per the tutorial packaging format with metadata, pinned images, and a validation manifest.
- Each tutorial's validation passes against the current release when run from a clean user project in a workbench opened with the tutorial notebook.
- Each tutorial records the image versions it was tested with (pinned per the packaging format).
- Tutorial content is complete for a new user: no step assumes platform knowledge beyond what the tutorial has introduced.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**: Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys, each tested against the current release. This epic delivers five of the six tutorials (the notebook journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first deployment, first RAG app); the first-pipeline tutorial is delivered by the pipeline tutorial epic.

# Document tutorial gallery usage and the tutorial contribution process

## Description

This epic authors the user-facing documentation for the tutorial gallery: how to use the gallery and launch tutorials, and how to contribute new tutorials. It is the documentation work stream of the tutorial gallery strategy and runs last, so the documentation describes what was actually built.

## Scope

Content outline:

- **Using the tutorial gallery** (user guide topic):
  - What the tutorial gallery is and where to find it in the Dashboard.
  - Browsing curated tutorials and understanding journey metadata.
  - Launching a notebook tutorial into your project (workbench with the notebook).
  - Launching a pipeline tutorial into your project (pipeline import).
  - What to expect during and after launch; where the tutorial lives afterwards.
- **Contributing new tutorials** (contribution-process topic):
  - The tutorial packaging format as an authoring contract: metadata, pinned images, validation manifest.
  - How to author, package, and version a tutorial.
  - How tutorial validation works and what must pass before a tutorial is curated.
  - How to submit a tutorial for curation (documentation of the process only — no submission tooling this release, per the strategy's out-of-scope statement).
- Screenshots and captions reflecting the shipped gallery, refreshed as part of this epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A published documentation topic covers using the tutorial gallery: finding it, browsing, and launching both notebook and pipeline tutorials.
- A published documentation topic covers the contribution process for new tutorials: packaging, versioning, validation, and submission for curation.
- Documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented gallery and the shipped tutorials (reviewed by or with the engineering owners of the gallery and tutorial content).
- Screenshots and steps match the shipped product behavior.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)**: Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution process for new tutorials. This epic delivers HLR-4 in full.

## Criterion Details

### 1. HLR Coverage (2/2)

All four HLRs map to epics: HLR-1 → E002 (gallery + one-click launch),

first-pipeline tutorial in E004 — together all six), HLR-3 → E001,

Priority inheritance is correct: E001 carries only HLR-3 (P1) but is
correctly scored P0 because it transitively enables all P0 work (E002, E003,
E004 all depend on it). E005 is `docs-authoring` and is exempt from priority
inheritence; its P1 derives from the strategy's `priority: Major` per the
documented exception, correctly noted in the matrix. No epic maps to HLRs at
multiple priority levels, so no priority-collapse concern arises.

### 2. DAG Coherence (2/2)

Frontmatter `dependencies` and the summary DAG diagram match exactly in both
directions (E002/E003/E004 ← E001; E005 ← E001/E002/E003/E004), arrows drawn
dependency → dependent per convention. No cycles; no edges reference
nonexistent epics; no branch files exist and none are needed.

Edges are justified: E001 → E002/E003/E004 are Rule 13 build-against-artifact
edges (the packaging format is a genuine contract both the gallery code and
all tutorial content build against — a real artifact dependency, not a
configuration reference). E002/E003/E004 run parallel as required (different
repos/teams, no shared artifact beyond the already-serialized format), and
E002's need for a packaged tutorial to verify launch end-to-end is satisfied
by E001's reference package, so no missing edge to E003/E004 exists. All
four Implementation → docs-authoring (Rule 11) edges are present. No
konflux-onboarding, license-validation, or repo-onboarding epics exist, so
Rules 7/8/10 parallelism is not implicated.

One minor nit: the summary frontmatter declares `critical_path_length: 4`,
but the longest path in the DAG is 3 epics (E001 → E002/E003/E004 → E005).
Within the S/M heuristics either way; the field is simply off by one.

### 3. Epic Boundaries (2/2)

Component/team tuples are clean and canonical: E001/E002 Dashboard /
RHOAI Dashboard, E003 Notebooks / Workbenches, E004 Data Science Pipelines /
RHOAI Pipelines, E005 Documentation / RHOAI Documentation. E001 spans

span is explicitly recorded in Health Warnings and the epic is assigned a
single canonical component with one owning team — one logical change, not a
multi-team bundle.

The E003/E004 split is along component/team lines (Workbenches vs RHOAI

content authoring: E001's reference package is part of proving the format it

E003's size overage (five release-tested tutorials, above the ~2-week
guideline) is handled exactly per the rubric: acknowledged in Health Warnings
as one logical change (single authoring/validation pass over one format) with
a concrete re-split trigger recorded (estimate overrun >50% or any tutorial
needing more than one release-test cycle → split by journey group). A
triggered, justified overage scores 2.
